skill.name: iso-13485-certification
skill.description: Helps medical device teams prepare ISO 13485 Quality Management System documentation. It supports gap analysis, Quality Manual drafting, procedure creation, and audit readiness planning.
skill.summary: Prepare ISO 13485 QMS documents, gap analyses, templates, and audit readiness plans.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Static analysis was dominated by false positives from ISO 13485 vocabulary, Markdown backticks, and normal documentation references. I confirmed one medium issue: gap_analyzer.py writes to a user-supplied output path without an overwrite guard. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, network calls, or malicious intent.

remediation.issue: Unrestricted report output path in scripts/gap_analyzer.py.
remediation.suggestion: Validate --output against the working directory and refuse to overwrite existing files without explicit confirmation.

remediation.issue: Script execution guidance lacks a data handling safety note.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users the analyzer reads local files and should run only on selected QMS folders.

content.value_statement: ISO 13485 certification requires many controlled QMS documents and clear evidence. This skill gives teams templates, gap analysis guidance, and prioritized documentation plans.
actual_capabilities: Runs a local gap analyzer against user-provided documentation directories.
Maps documents to ISO 13485:2016 clauses and required procedures.
Provides Quality Manual, CAPA, and document control templates.
Guides creation of Medical Device Files and QMS procedures.
Builds prioritized action plans from checklist and script results.
limitations: It does not replace certification body, legal, or regulatory advice.
Automated analysis checks document presence and keywords, not implementation quality.
The script reads local document text and writes an optional JSON report.
Templates require review by qualified quality and regulatory personnel.

use_cases.title: Start a New QMS
use_cases.description: Create the foundation documents, procedure sequence, and first implementation plan for ISO 13485 certification.
use_cases.target_user: Medical device startup founder or regulatory lead

use_cases.title: Assess Existing Documentation
use_cases.description: Compare current QMS files against required procedures and identify missing documents or weak evidence.
use_cases.target_user: Quality manager at an established manufacturer

use_cases.title: Prepare for Certification Audit
use_cases.description: Review manuals, procedures, records, and CAPA evidence before a registrar or customer audit.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new ISO 13485 program.
prompt_templates.prompt: We are starting ISO 13485 for a medical device company. Create a prioritized documentation plan with phases and key records.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Document Gaps
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request using an existing QMS document folder.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the QMS documents in my selected folder. Identify missing ISO 13485 procedures and summarize the highest priority gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a CAPA Procedure
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a controlled procedure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a CAPA procedure for our organization. Ask for roles, approval levels, timeframes, and root cause methods before drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Audit Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an ISO 13485 audit readiness plan that also considers FDA QMSR and EU MDR documentation expectations.

output_examples.input: We are a startup with no QMS documents. What should we create first?
output: Start with Quality Policy, Quality Objectives, Quality Manual, Document Control, and Record Control.
Then create CAPA, Complaint Handling, Internal Audit, Management Review, and Risk Management procedures.
Use a phased plan so each new procedure references approved foundation documents.

output_examples.input: We have procedures, but we do not know what is missing.
output: Run the gap analyzer on the selected QMS folder, then review the checklist manually.
Treat keyword matches as leads, not proof of compliance.
Prioritize missing complaint, CAPA, audit, supplier, and risk management procedures.

output_examples.input: Help me create a CAPA procedure for our device company.
output: The procedure should define initiation sources, investigation steps, root cause methods, actions, verification, and effectiveness checks.
It should assign role-based responsibilities and reference related complaint, audit, and nonconforming product processes.
Before approval, replace placeholders and confirm records, forms, and retention rules.

best_practices: Start with scope, exclusions, and document control before drafting detailed procedures.
Customize templates to real company processes and assigned roles.
Have qualified quality and regulatory staff approve final documents.
anti_patterns: Do not copy ISO text without describing actual procedures and responsibilities.
Do not treat keyword gap analysis as proof of implementation.
Do not publish templates with placeholders, missing approvals, or inconsistent references.

faq.question: Can this skill certify my company to ISO 13485?
faq.answer: No. It helps prepare documentation, but certification requires implementation and assessment by an accredited certification body.

faq.question: Does it include templates?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes templates for a Quality Manual, CAPA procedure, and document control procedure.

faq.question: Can it analyze my existing documents?
faq.answer: Yes. The included script scans a selected local folder and reports likely missing procedures.

faq.question: Is the gap analyzer enough for audit readiness?
faq.answer: No. Use it as a first pass, then verify implementation, records, training, and process evidence manually.

faq.question: Does it support FDA QMSR planning?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance discusses QMSR alignment and Medical Device File planning, but regulatory review is still required.

faq.question: Who should review the generated documents?
faq.answer: A qualified quality, regulatory, or compliance professional should review and approve all controlled documents.
